# Capturing a source while it exists

A useful research note keeps the page address, author when known, capture date and a short exact excerpt beside the claim it supports. Save an allowed local snapshot if the source is likely to change. A bare bookmark can later lead to different wording or a missing page.

The note should say what was observed at capture time. Separate the source's words from an interpretation written later. When revisiting a changed page, retain the original citation and add the newer observation rather than silently replacing the evidence. Tags can help navigation, but do not preserve what a source actually said.
